title: Ephemeral Surge Controller: operator visibility and rate settlement for temporary boosts
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
We need a new controller and operator surface that manages ephemeral burst allocations (surge pools and temporary boosts) while providing transparent, auditable rate settlement for overage billing. Current behavior is opaque to operators and customers during bursts: the platform auto-grants short-lived headroom, billing can appear inconsistent, and SREs lack a single place to observe burst decisions and rollback policies.

Goals:
- Introduce an Ephemeral Surge Controller (ESC) responsible for validating, granting, and expiring temporary capacity boosts from a pool of reserved nodes.
- Provide operator visibility: real-time dashboard + event stream describing decisions (grant, deny, preempt, expire) and the rationale (policy, owner override, cost tier).
- Implement a rate settlement design that deterministically attributes tokens / minutes to either committed capacity, burst credits, or overage buckets for invoicing and customer-facing invoices.
- Ensure predictable SLO impact: bursts must not violate per-tenant latency SLOs for committed lanes; ESC should apply graceful degradation when necessary.
- Keep runtime performance overhead minimal: decision path must be <5ms tail in control plane paths.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not add new pricing tiers or modify existing committed-contract economics.

Design sketch:
1) Surge pool model: maintain a named pool resource with metadata (capacity units, expiry policy, owner, budget window). Pools are finite and backfilled by autoscaler when utilization low.
2) Grant flow: request arrives at routing layer when committed capacity saturated. Routing consults ESC which evaluates policies: customer policy (allowBurst: boolean/limit), billing mode (pre-paid credits vs invoice-overage), global headroom, and recent burst history (cooldown). ESC returns an allocation token with lifetime and attribution tags.
3) Attribution tags: each allocation token contains a settlement tag: [committed, burst_credit_id, overage_bucket_id]. Settlement tags are emitted to the billing ledger at allocation time and reconciliation events at expiry.
4) Operator surface: new console page under Dedicated -> Burst Management that lists active grants, recent decisions with reasons, and a replayable event log (links to PR artifacts and supporting traces). Ability to revoke grants and force preemption.
5) Billing settlement: billing ledger receives allocation and expiry events, and a nightly reconciler calculates final attribution and generates proforma lines for invoices. For overage, we apply an amortized smoothing window (configurable, default 24h) to avoid sharp invoice surprises for customers.
6) Safe-fallback: if ESC is unavailable, requests fall back to a conservative limiter that denies burst and returns a controlled 429 with an explicit retry-after and an indicator for client-side degradation.

Trade-offs and decisions considered:
- Centralized ESC vs decentralized per-region controllers: centralized gives stronger consistency for billing, but higher latencies and a single failure domain; decided on region-scoped ESC instances with a global reconciliation job.
- Immediate billing vs reconciled billing: immediate is simpler for accounting but risks noisy invoices. We chose reconciliation with amortized smoothing to reduce customer churn while keeping auditability.
- Strong attribution tagging increases control plane message size; we compress tags and avoid synchronously persisting heavy metadata on the hot path.

Acceptance criteria (must meet all):
- ESC grants/denies operate within 5ms median additional control-plane latency on canary region.
- Console surface shows active grants with per-allocation reason and owner; operators can revoke allocations and receive audit log entries.
- Billing ledger receives allocation and expiry events; nightly reconciler produces stable attribution lines and test invoice for sample tenants.
- Reconciler smoothing window default works end-to-end and avoids >40% delta between provisional and reconciled invoice lines for tested bursts.
- Chaos test: simulated ESC instance crash triggers fallback limiter and no silent capacity leaks (no customers are billed for allocations that never materialized).

Implementation plan (phases):
- Phase 1 (prototype, 2 weeks): region-scoped ESC service, simple policy engine, allocation token format, mock billing event emitter, and a lightweight operator CLI.
- Phase 2 (observability, 2 weeks): console page, event stream, timeline, and audit entries; integrate traces and link to existing trace ids.
- Phase 3 (billing + reconciliation, 3 weeks): wire allocation/expiry events into billing ledger, implement nightly reconciler and amortized smoothing, generate proforma invoices for canary tenants.
- Phase 4 (hardening + rollout, 2 weeks): canary deploy to low-risk region, run load tests, measure latency and billing deltas, and expand to other regions with feature flag.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for policy permutations, expiry, and cooldown windows.
- Integration test with autoprospecting autoscaler to ensure pools refill correctly.
- Load test: synthetic traffic ramp to saturate committed lanes and trigger ESC grants from many tenants; assert <1% incorrect attribution and control-plane latency targets.
- Billing reconciliation test: simulate 7 days of bursts and assert smoothing metrics and invoice stability.

Rollout and communication:
- Start with internal canary tenants (engineering, a small set of opt-in customers).
- Run a customer-facing notification explaining amortized smoothing and how burst attribution appears on invoices.
- Provide a public support playbook for contested invoices referencing the ESC event stream and allocation ids.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Exact amortization formula for smoothing (linear vs weighted by duration) — propose weighted-by-duration for fairness.
- How to surface burst history to customers in their billing portal without exposing operator-only metadata.
- Limits on total per-customer burst debt before we force pre-paid lockout.

2026-02-27 - Priya (SRE): Load test w/ 500 tenants in canary region. Control plane tail spiked to 18ms under GC pressure. Action: tune ESC GC and region instance memory limits; follow-up ENG-77510 created.

2026-03-04 - Devon (Billing): Reviewed settlement tags. Requested explicit field for "billing_class" to disambiguate pre-paid vs invoice-overage. Added to token schema. Updated PR with compatibility tests.

2026-03-08 - Design review (Asha): Console mock approved with minor copy edits. Need to show 'estimated invoice impact' per grant in the UI. Design ticket DES-212 to follow up for copy and UX microcopy.

2026-03-10 - QA: Nightly reconciler produced proforma invoices for sample tenants (tenant-alpha, tenant-gamma). Delta between provisional and reconciled lines: 18% and 9% respectively - within target. QA note: add a test for a 60-minute burst to ensure smoothing holds on longer tails.
